goals.title: Run tighter client calls
goals.smart: Finish a speaking/facilitation program by end of Q4 2026 and make focused, well-run client calls repeatable.

measurables.label: Program picked & started by end of July 2026; then finished by end of Q4 (course) or attended regularly with two prepared talks given (Toastmasters).
measurables.detail: No program start is on record as of Aug 6, so the end-of-July target has passed unmet. Worth confirming whether a course or Toastmasters was chosen offline — if so, log it here.

measurables.label: Listen back to one of your own calls each month; note one thing to keep and one to change.
measurables.detail: No monthly listen-back note recorded yet. This dashboard now gives you talk-share and a coaching note for every client call, so the listen-back is one step: pick a call below and jot one keep + one change.

measurables.label: By the next review, point to moments you caught yourself drifting and pulled out fast.
measurables.detail: Early receipts are here: on Avalon (7/2) you named it live (“I feel like I keep cutting you off”). Client talk-share is also easing downward across July — a high of 79% on Jul 1, down to 24% on the FWW call and a 0% hand-off to a specialist by Jul 8. Keep the receipts building toward the next review.

goals.title: Protect evenings & weekends
goals.smart: Get the week near ~32 hours inside a set window (~9:00–5:30 ET), with late nights and weekends the rare exception. The goal is to work less, not log less — accurate time logging stays the expectation.

measurables.label: A working window (~9:00–5:30 ET) + a real shutdown habit in place.
measurables.detail: Weekends are protected (0 weekend days logged in each of the last three weeks) and hours land close to target (~34h on full weeks, a touch over 32). The evening edge is hard to read: only 4 of 165 entries are timer-tracked, so ‘late evening’ really means when time got logged — and those cluster around 10pm ET, which looks more like end-of-day logging than late work.

measurables.label: No more than two evenings a week past the window; weekends off by default.
measurables.detail: Weekends off is landing — 0 weekend days across the last three weeks. The ‘≤2 late evenings’ half can't be confirmed from Productive: 96% of entries are hand-logged (not timed) and the log times bunch in the evening (a 10pm ET spike), which reads as batch logging more than evening work. Timer-tracking one week would settle it.

measurables.label: Monthly trend reviewed (the pattern, not an exact count).
measurables.detail: The pattern is now on the dashboard and easy to review: hours holding ~34h on full weeks (just over the 32 target), weekends trending to zero, and a lighter week around the 7/27–7/28 sick days. Evening activity is frequent but is a logging-time signal, not confirmed work.

goals.title: Launch Stef's Corner
goals.smart: A recurring thought-leadership series under Stef's name, on a steady cadence, making complex nonprofit marketing and technical topics easy to act on.

measurables.label: Format, home, and focus area decided by end of July 2026.
measurables.detail: Format (a written series), home (Blog + LinkedIn), and focus (making complex nonprofit marketing + technical topics easy to act on) are set, with 8 topics queued below. If this was formally locked by end of July, M1 is met.

measurables.label: First piece published by end of Q3 2026.
measurables.detail: Nothing published yet — all 8 topics are in ‘Idea’. On track if a draft starts in the next few weeks; the ENgrid-rebuild and donation-tracking topics are the most ready to write from recent work.

measurables.label: One piece every 6–8 weeks after that (4–6 over the year); track reach lightly.
measurables.detail: Cadence begins once the first piece ships. Track reach lightly — views, shares, conversations.

calls.title: SMART Goals - Progress Check-in with Bryan

calls.feedback: Strong facilitation. You spoke about a quarter of the time and gave Romain real room to think through the budget out loud, and you did not talk over anyone. Nice move asking Romain what would actually help him, then letting him answer rather than filling the silence.

calls.title: 4Site / Avalon - PCF biweekly check in
calls.feedback: Warm and consultative. You opened with genuine rapport, confirmed the Meta fix with real evidence (the 12 events you saw in Events Manager), and were honest about the Conversion API trade-off instead of overselling it. You were mindful of time too, flagging 'I want to make sure we have enough time' before handing to Wynn for the SEO review. Two things to watch: the Microsoft Ads piece turned into live troubleshooting on the call (reading out the data-layer variable, 'let me see where'), which ate a few minutes. A cleaner move is 'let me triage this offline and confirm back' earlier, which you did land on eventually. And a couple of fixes were framed tentatively ('I would have to double-check if this works'); a confident 'here is the fix, I will verify and confirm' reads as more assured without overpromising. You gave Chris plenty of space and did not talk over anyone.

calls.title: 4Site / CLF biweekly check in
calls.feedback: Really warm and consultative. You built genuine rapport and were transparent about your process and hours, which clients trust. Watch the length of the technical explanations: the Looker Studio and Engaging Networks API update ran close to three minutes and circled back on the API-metering detail, when the client mostly needed the headline and next step ('I am working out how to pull EN data automatically, I am confirming with EN support today on what their API allows, and I would like three to four hours next week'). The opening also ran a few minutes of catch-up before business, lovely on a light agenda but worth trimming on a full one. You gave Chelsea real space to lay out the email data she wants, and closed by confirming priorities, which is exactly right.

calls.title: FWW + 4Site 1st Tuesday check in
calls.feedback: A well-run, warm check-in where you played the supporting expert well. Sebrinia drove the agenda and you came in exactly where your expertise mattered (the Remember Me scope, the flexible 'separate project or add-on' option for the unsubscribe work, budget-conscious as always), and the Chicago retreat coffee/dinner invite was a genuine relationship move. One small pattern to keep an eye on: when the post-ID data question came up you thought out loud across several turns (page path vs page ID, Watch vs Action) before landing on your hypothesis. That instinct is good, but a crisper 'I spotted some pages not mapping, I think it is the Action site, I will confirm and follow up' gives the client the same confidence without the live working-through. You gave everyone plenty of space and the call stayed on time.

calls.title: NWF + 4Site 1st Tuesday Check In
calls.feedback: Clean and well-paced. Your analytics update was clear and appropriately high level, you were transparent about the one wrinkle (nwfaction.org running a different CMS) without over-dwelling, and you closed with 'any questions?' You were proactive and consultative on the UTM training, giving Stephanie concrete guidance on what to bring. You gave Bryan and the client plenty of room and the meeting ended on time. Keep doing what you did here: you led with the outcome and timeline first, then the caveat, which is exactly the crisper structure worth carrying into the longer walkthroughs. A model check-in.

calls.title: PaintCare + 4Site biweekly check in
calls.feedback: A strong, honest walkthrough. You set the right expectation up front ('still in progress, caveat that with leadership'), explained metrics in plain language, and when the odd URLs came up you did not guess, you said 'I will diagnose this and get back to you,' which builds trust. You also turned Brett's questions into a clear action list (addresses on site names, fix the not-set, an exportable report). The one thing to own next time is the clock: Sebrinia had to call the time check and you ran over, rushing the exportability question at the end. Brett had a hard stop and a leadership meeting to prep, so a tighter frame up front ('we have 25 minutes, let me hit the overview and the two things you will get asked about, then go deeper next time') would let you steer the depth instead of touring every panel. Brett drove a lot of the questions, which is great engagement, so guiding the pace is the lever, not talking less.

calls.title: 4Site / Stupski monthly check in
calls.feedback: Genuinely warm, and Claire clearly values working with you (she credited you for the 'put up the FAQs you want people to ask' advice). You delegated well to Tayo with the shared-spreadsheet handoff so you two would not double up, asked a sharp question about how she curated the FAQs, and closed on budget. Two clear growth spots, both about prep and pacing: the personal catch-up at the top ran about five minutes before business (lovely, and worth saving some of it for the coffee/dinner you offered), and the Google Ads account setup was done live on the call with a lot of fumbling ('why is my screen,' hunting for old campaigns, 'let me see if it saved'), which ate close to ten minutes. Setting up and verifying the account beforehand, then walking Claire through a checklist, turns that stretch from watching you configure into a confident hand-off. You gave her plenty of space throughout and never talked over her.

calls.title: 4Site / Avalon - PCF biweekly check in call
calls.feedback: This was a deep, collaborative debugging session with a technical counterpart, which changes the calculus. The live back-and-forth troubleshooting is far more appropriate here than it would be on a presentation call. Your command of the detail is obvious, you were refreshingly honest about the uncertainty ('it honestly should not be this hard'), and you landed on a clear plan: the WP Code plugin to remove the workaround, a dedicated test UTM, and process of elimination. Two gentle notes. The session ran long and over time with a lot of thinking-aloud, so for the trickiest bits a 'let me run five clean tests, capture what fires, and send you a two-line summary' keeps it from sprawling. And the self-deprecating asides ('I feel like I do not know anything anymore') read as camaraderie with a peer like Chris, but save them for exactly that audience; with a less technical client they can undercut the confidence you have earned. You closed by confirming the SEO-audit timing, which was the right instinct.
